steps.title: What sorting does
steps.content: Sorting arranges data in a chosen order, usually ascending or descending. A good algorithm also considers input size, memory and whether equal items keep their relative order.

steps.title: Understand bubble sort
steps.prompt: In one left-to-right pass of bubble sort on [4,1,3,2], which value is guaranteed to reach the final position?
steps.explanation: The largest value moves right whenever an adjacent pair is swapped, so 4 reaches the final position after one full pass.

steps.title: Compare common algorithms
steps.content: Bubble, selection and insertion sort are O(n²) in average/worst cases. Merge sort is O(n log n) and uses extra memory. Quicksort is O(n log n) on average but O(n²) in the worst case.
steps.tip: For small or nearly sorted arrays, insertion sort can perform well despite O(n²) worst-case complexity.

steps.title: Choose the complexity
steps.prompt: What is the average time complexity of merge sort?
steps.explanation: Merge sort splits the input into log n levels and processes n elements per level: O(n log n).

steps.title: Stability and in-place sorting
steps.content: A stable sort keeps equal-key items in their original relative order. An in-place algorithm uses little extra memory beyond the input array. These are separate properties.

questions.prompt: Which algorithm repeatedly swaps adjacent out-of-order items?
questions.explanation: Bubble sort compares adjacent values and swaps when they are out of order.

questions.prompt: What is the average time complexity of merge sort?
questions.explanation: Merge sort has O(n log n) time in best, average and worst cases.

questions.prompt: Which algorithm is usually efficient on small, nearly sorted arrays?
questions.explanation: Insertion sort can run close to O(n) on nearly sorted input.

questions.prompt: What does a stable sort guarantee?
questions.explanation: Stability preserves the original order of records with equal keys.
Poor pivots can create highly unbalanced partitions, giving O(n²) worst-case time.
